schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The door to the open-question lane: a decision Akien has to make is a QUESTION bound to the ticket (or intention) that needs it, written to `CairnCommons/questions/open-<12hex>.json` through the artifact door (verbs `question` and `answer`), standing in his operator inbox until answered; the answer IS the decision and is recorded verbatim on the question. `open_question(ticket, question, why_it_blocks, born_of=)` opens one (a question ends with '?'; a born_of must exist). `answer(qid, words, spawned=[...])` resolves it, records the caller class the artifact door measured (cc when CC records his chat words, akien when he answers from his own shell), and opens each spawned question `born_of` it on the same ticket — the loop goes around until the ticket has every answer. `spawned` is REQUIRED (ticket bc7b64626405, 2026-09-14): `[]` records that the answer bore nothing, a list records the ids it bore; None is refused, because an answer that does not say what it spawned is a silence no inspector can read. THE LINK HAS TWO ENDS, WRITTEN IN ONE ACT: `open_question` writes the question record (verb `question`) and, when the ticket id resolves to a file under `<commons>/tickets/`, appends the id to that ticket's `questions` list (verb `cast`) — a question about a ticket is named by the ticket. `rebind(ticket_id)` moves every question bound to the ticket's `intent_berth` path onto the id and writes the ticket-side end (fired at /sorted step 5, once the file exists). The build inspector's sieve `question_links_agree` reds the two ends disagreeing — an id a ticket lists whose record is absent or names another ticket, a question whose ticket does not list it back, a spawned id with no record born_of it, a question still bound to a berth some filed ticket carries. `open_for(ticket)` is what the BUILDME entry gate reads: `build_inspector.buildme_has_no_open_questions` reds while any unresolved question cites the ticket, and `transitions.inspect_entry` refuses the TICKETME→BUILDME crossing on that red. CLI: `cairn question open|answer|list|show`.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: on 2026-09-14 Akien asked 'why are we still doing rulings? we replaced that with questions that would show up in my inbox.' Measured that day: rulings had never been retired in the record — CLAUDE.md, six skills, the Stop hook and CC's own memory all said `cairn ruling open`, five packets had been opened since 2026-09-08 — while the questions lane (ruled 2026-08-01, edges-become-open-questions) existed, was read by the inbox, and had been empty since 2026-08-27. The replacement lived in his head; this tool is its translation. His design, verbatim: 'what was the ruling should now be part of the ticketing or intention recording process. slash sorted should lead to questions, and if i can't answer then right then, for whatever reason, they become open questions in the inbox. and yes, the answer to the question is the decision... ASSUMING THE ANSWER DOES NOT LEAD TO YET MORE QUESTIONS. If the answer does, we keep going around until you have all the answers you need.' And: 'we want to squeeze out the decisions toward the front of the process.' WHY A QUESTION AND NOT A PACKET: a ruling was a standalone artifact CC drafted and he confirmed — the decision lived apart from the work that needed it, and CC drafted the binary. A question is bound to the ticket by id, opened where the gap is found (/sorted), and his words are the whole record; there is nothing to draft. WHY THE GATE IS THE EXIT CONDITION: 'until you have all the answers you need' is prose until a crossing refuses; the BUILDME gate makes it physics, and the ticket that built it (9adc6fddf185) was the first measured by it — its own four questions had to be answered before it crossed. WHY BOTH CALLER CLASSES: his answer to open-690330e1cfa6 — 'yes it can come via chat. and you can also say are you sure? ... those are all fine' — the class is journaled either way, never used to refuse. WHY decisions/ STAYS: his answer to open-68aabd7eb2e0 ('yeah') — read-only record, citable by path, no migration; `cairn ruling open` refuses from now on and points here.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.question import question as Q; Q.open_question(ticket, q, why, born_of=None); Q.answer(qid, words, spawned=[...]); Q.rebind(ticket_id); Q.open_for(ticket); Q.for_ticket(ticket); Q.render_tree(records)`. CLI: `cairn question open --ticket <id> "<q>" --why "<what it blocks>" [--born-of <qid>]`, `cairn question answer <qid> "<his words>" --spawned none | --spawned "<q?>" ...` (required; `none` is a system word and folds case), `cairn question rebind <ticket-id>`, `cairn question list [<ticket>]` (with a ticket: the tree, question → spawned → spawned), `cairn question show <qid>`. The inbox renders every unresolved question with its ticket and text (`cairn operator_inbox`, QUESTIONS section). `cairn operator show artifact <ticket>` renders the same tree under QUESTIONS. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_question.py` and `python3 cairn/tools/question/proofs/test_question_links.py`. Scratch world: `CAIRN_QUESTIONS_DIR` or the `root=` kwarg.
entry: Written 2026-09-14 under ticket 9adc6fddf185 (idea 2026-09-14-why-are-we-still-doing-rulings-we; intent berth intent-20260914T110302-5cac1c85f228; sorted berth sorted-20260914T110400-d54062eb0231). Patterns cited, not grafted: the record shape is the open lane's existing schema (CairnCommons/questions/_charter+why.json) with answer fields added; the write rides the artifact door as every record does; the gate lane is the same `_sieve_lane` shape as buildme_rides_the_intent and buildme_rides_the_sorted. Extended 2026-09-14 under ticket bc7b64626405 (Akien: 'if a question is about a ticket, it should have a bidirectional link ... in some jsonic way that's not prose'; intent berth intent-20260914T145018-3aad6f4abb5a): the ticket-side end, the required `spawned`, `rebind`, the sieve, the tree renderer.
state_and_history: The questions are the COMMONS' records (jurisdiction: questions/*.json), journaled by the artifact door and committed with the commons. This tool keeps no state.json or history.json beside its code; the ticket's voyage is its history.
filed_edges: (a) A QUESTION RAISED AT /intent HAS NO TICKET ID YET. It binds to the intent berth path until /sorted casts the ticket. CLOSED 2026-09-14 by ticket bc7b64626405: `open_for` counts a question bound to the ticket's `intent_berth` (the gate holds either way), `cairn question rebind <id>` at /sorted step 5 renames it and writes the ticket-side end, and the sieve `question_links_agree` reds one left on a berth a filed ticket carries.

(b) THE GATE READS ONE DIRECTORY. A question filed anywhere but CairnCommons/questions/ (or CAIRN_QUESTIONS_DIR) is not a question to the gate. One spelling, by design; a second store would be the drift.

(c) 'ANSWERED' IS A FIELD, NOT A JUDGEMENT. An answer of 'are you sure?' resolves the question as written — the tool cannot tell a decision from a deflection. CLOSED AS FAR AS PHYSICS REACHES 2026-09-14 by ticket bc7b64626405: the answer must SAY what it spawned (`spawned: []` or the ids), so a deflection that bore a question and recorded none is a false claim the record carries, not a silence; what stays is that the claim is CC's to make honestly.

(d) THE HISTORICAL RULINGS ARE NOT REBOUND. decisions/ stays read-only and citable by path; sieves that accept 'a ruling in the same act' now also accept an answered question id, but no ruling was rewritten as a question (his answer to open-68aabd7eb2e0).
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_question.py (open through the door and the inbox shows it; answer resolves, journals the caller class, spawned questions born_of, and an answer that does not say what it spawned refused; the BUILDME crossing refused with an open question and passing once answered — with the gate reverted the crossing goes through, the hollow tooth; `cairn ruling open` non-zero; the Stop hook gone; zero skills say open a ruling; the two inspector sieves accept an answered question id). proof gate — proofs/test_question_links.py (ticket bc7b64626405: open writes both ends and journals both; spawned required and recorded; a berth-bound question holds the gate and rebind renames it; the sieve `question_links_agree` reds each hand-break with one finding and reads the live corpus clean; the probe armed; CLI, renderer, wording, charter). Build gate — `buildme_has_no_open_questions` at the emit chokepoint. Inspector sieve — `question_links_agree` in build_inspector, scoped to this component's row, over the commons' questions and tickets. Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) `cairn question open --ticket <id> "<q>"` does not write open-<qid>.json through the artifact door, or the operator inbox does not list it under that ticket; (2) `cairn question answer` does not resolve the question, journal the caller class, or open each spawned question born_of it — or records an answer without `spawned` (bc7b64626405: an answer that does not say what it spawned is not a recorded claim); (3) a TICKETME ticket with one unresolved question crosses to BUILDME through the emit chokepoint, or a ticket whose questions are all answered is refused — and with the gate reverted the crossing must go through (the hollow tooth); (4) `cairn ruling open` exits zero, `ruling --hook` stands in the Stop hooks, or any skill tells CC to open a ruling; (6) [bc7b64626405] `cairn question open --ticket <id>` writes the question and the ticket's `questions` does not gain the id in the same act, or `question_links_agree` reads a ticket listing an id whose record is absent or names another ticket, a question whose ticket does not list it back, a spawned id with no record born_of it, or a berth-bound question a filed ticket carries — and reads green; or `cairn question rebind <id>` leaves a berth-bound question on the berth; (5) constraint_enforcement_holds or every_exemption_cites_a_ruling_or_an_impossibility refuses an answered question id as same-act evidence, or accepts a cite of neither. WRONG INTENT: a decision arrives that no ticket or intention can bind — then standalone decisions were a real class and decisions/ reopens as an intake.
proof: proofs/test_question.py — PROVES['9adc6fddf185'] one tooth per falsifier clause; sealed under the tester. probes/no_crossing_with_an_open_question.py — the WATCHME probe: counts BUILDME crossings after the gate exists against the open-question count at each, and every answer's caller class. proofs/test_question_links.py — PROVES['bc7b64626405'] one tooth per clause of the links ticket; sealed under the tester. probes/both_ends_agree.py — the WATCHME probe (a_question_and_its_ticket_name_each_other): runs `question_links_agree` over the live commons and counts the door's own question|answer journal events since the build; FIRES on a lack over a record the door itself wrote (WRONG-INTENT), ENOUGH at 50 events with zero lacks and 5 answers that spawned.
owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Its users: the /sorted and /intent skills (the openers), CC recording Akien's chat answers, Akien from his own shell, the operator inbox (reader), the frontier projector cairn/tools/edges (reader), the BUILDME entry gate (reader). The records are the commons' and are gated by the artifact door. CC writes the code and proofs; Akien answers.
traces_to: Law 1 (every answered question becomes structure — the answer rides the ticket that needed it, never re-derived)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — 'until you have all the answers' is a crossing gate, not discipline)
Law 6 (a tool has users; the records are the commons')
Law 9 (his head says what SHOULD BE — the question is how the build asks it, and the answer outranks every artifact)
decisions/2026-08-01-edges-become-open-questions (the lane this tool is the second tenant of)
provenance: Born 2026-09-14 from Akien's question 'why are we still doing rulings?'. The first thing done was to exercise the shape before the tool existed: the ticket's own four spec questions were opened as open-*.json through the artifact door, showed in his inbox, and were answered in chat and recorded verbatim — then the door, the gate and the retirement were built.
learns: Nothing of its own. The lane's throughput is what the WATCHME probe measures (crossings vs open-question count, spawned depth, caller class per answer) for the counting learning block (5a4ec289bf15) to read who answers what. The second probe (both_ends_agree) counts whether the two ends of the link ever disagreed outside the proof.
how_it_learns: It does not; a question store has no parameters to adjust. The probes beside it (probes/no_crossing_with_an_open_question.py, probes/both_ends_agree.py) report the lane's throughput on each crossing and each answer; what learns from the report is the counting learning block, not this tool.
